on_record.summary: The Moscow venue of the V-A-C Foundation, which he founded in 2009; he transferred GES-2 to his daughter in 2023.
His V-A-C Foundation built GES-2, at a cost put at around $300 million in 2018, a figure he said in 2019 had doubled.
After the 2022 invasion V-A-C's artistic director and music curator resigned and Ragnar Kjartansson withdrew his launch show.
Subsidiaries of Novatek, the gas producer he chairs, partnered GES-2’s first regional festival, in Kostroma.
The V-A-C Foundation is still listed among its funders.
Novatek, the gas producer he runs, paid for the renovation before the 2021 Architecture Biennale.
Is listed as a private patron, for exhibition projects in Samara.
Named for his daughter Victoria.
Founded in 2005 and owned by Mikhelson.

Philippa de Menil, heir to the Schlumberger oil fortune, co-founded the Dia Art Foundation in 1974 with her money. The foundation runs the museum.
Philippa de Menil, heir to the Schlumberger oil fortune, co-founded the Dia Art Foundation in 1974 with her money. The foundation runs the gallery.
John and Dominique de Menil founded it through their Menil Foundation, set up in 1954, which governs it. Dominique's family fortune came from Schlumberger.
SLB is a corporate sponsor at $25,000 and above.
SLB is in the Dadu Founding Family, whose members give QAR 3.65 million or more (Marhaba.qa, 2023, updated 2024).

Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts

on_record.summary: A Gallery Partner, with Bloomberg Philanthropies and Bank of America (October 2026).
LG Electronics România was a sponsor in October 2023.
Its name is on the MMCA x LG OLED Series, which it sponsors under a multi-year partnership. The first show ran from August 2025.
Named as a partner of the museum and of the exhibition Diamond Chariot: Buddhist Art of Russia.
A yearly sponsor, with Neuroth and Dorotheum.
Runs, with the Fukutake Foundation, all the art on Naoshima, Teshima and Inujima, under its own name.
Began on Naoshima with a campsite in 1989, opened Benesse House, a hotel and museum, in 1992, and started the Art House Project in 1998.
Part of Benesse Art Site Naoshima, the art the company runs with the Fukutake Foundation under its own name.
Soichiro Fukutake chose the three artists the museum shows, so that each work has room.
Paid for by Soichiro Fukutake’s foundation, which runs on dividends from its shares in Benesse Holdings (The Peak, 2016).
Hideaki Fukutake, who chairs the board of Benesse Holdings, has chaired the Fukutake Foundation, which runs the museum, since January 2023. Soichiro Fukutake is the foundation's honorary chairman.
Soichiro Fukutake, honorary adviser of Benesse Holdings, is the festival’s general producer.
Funds it through the Fukutake Foundation, the family’s own investments and Benesse, beside government backing (English Wikipedia).
Launched it as a public-private partnership with the prefectural and municipal governments (English Wikipedia).
Soichiro Fukutake, honorary chairman of the Fukutake Foundation, is listed as the festival’s Honorary Adviser.
Hideaki Fukutake, chairman of the Fukutake Foundation, is a vice president of the executive committee, which the governor of Kagawa heads.
Dulux Australia, part of DuluxGroup, which Nippon Paint owns, is listed as a sponsor.
Dulux paint coloured the walls of the 2016 show Painting. More Painting, credited as exhibition colours by Dulux in Ticking Flat Acrylic and White Flat Acrylic.
Dulux is a 2026 partner. In Indonesia it is an AkzoNobel joint venture that Nippon Paint agreed in October 2026 to buy.
Dulux is listed as a partner. In Pakistan it is the brand of Akzo Nobel Pakistan, which AkzoNobel sold to the Packages Group in September 2026.
AkzoNobel, the Biennale's Color Partner for its 2020 edition, unveiled its 2020 Color of the Year, Tranquil Dawn, with the Lahore Biennale at the Wazir Khan Baradari.
Dulux New Zealand, owned by Nippon Paint through DuluxGroup, was listed as a current sponsor on the museum’s Partner with us page in January 2025.

Named among the museum's donors.

A founding member of the foundation. It gave €600,000 in 2025, the same annual sum under an agreement that runs to 2026.
A founding member of the foundation; its designee Francesca Gostinelli joined the board in May 2026.
Named as mobility partner in the 2024/25 business report.
Sponsors the membership programme.
Mercedes-Benz Werk Düsseldorf is a room sponsor (Saalpate) of the permanent collection, a commitment of at least three years.
Named among the gallery's top partners in the 2024/25 annual report.
Agnes Gund co-founded it in 1968 as The New Gallery.
Agnes Gund is a Champion, the top tier of PS1 donors.
The staff cottage called the “Twin A’s” carries her gift. She is also a campaign donor.
Gave $50,000 or more, as a Benefactor.
The late Lord Sainsbury and Sir Timothy Sainsbury are Fellows of the Ashmolean, its roll of major benefactors.
Lord Sainsbury and his brothers Simon and Tim paid almost 50 million pounds for the Sainsbury Wing, opened in 1991, which carries their name.
Alex Sainsbury is a trustee of the charitable company that runs it.
Founded by Alex Sainsbury, who bought the two houses in 2004 and opened the gallery in 2009.
Alex Sainsbury and the Glass-House Trust he settled gave £1.2m of its £1.54m income in 2024-25, with no public grants.
The ConocoPhillips Gallery on the second floor, which shows contemporary Alaska Native art, carries its name.
ConocoPhillips Alaska is on the museum's 2022 contributors list.
